metadata.title: Walker-TANK: Particles, Strips and the Game
metadata.audience: CSYE7270 students adding particle effects to small games with Walker + Claude Code
metadata.note: godot-gamedev walker mode, assignment-focused film (A6 particles only). New 4K fixture captures on a scratch copy only; the student's own play recording; no paid API, no upload, no game change.

beats.role_note: walker B00. Illustrative reconstruction of a Walker prompt; not the original chat.
beats.narration_text: Hola, this is Liam, in for Bear. Assignment Six gave walker tank two particle effects. The prompt is reconstructed.

show.event: result lines: reconstruction label, both effects, revision

props.command: Please use Walker to convert my game design document about walker-TANK — a 2D top-down tank battle — into two particle effects: a burst where a shell hits cover, and damage smoke that follows each tank's health.
output: A: cover hit burst · 3 × CPUParticles2D · B: damage smoke · GPUParticles2D

beats.role_note: walker B01: misconception corrected — particles as decoration -> each effect carries one message.

qc.sparse_reason: hesitant writer types line by line

beats.narration_text: A shell hits a wall. A tank gets hurt. Particles aren't decoration. Each one carries a message.

show.event: typing starts in the lead silence

props.text:
A shell hits a wall.
A hurt tank smokes.
Particles are decoration.

beats.role_note: Both effects as 4K fixture captures, side by side, with their jobs, events and conditions.
beats.narration_text: Effect A, the cover hit burst: your shell landed on that wall, right there. It fires from take hit, line forty. Effect B, damage smoke: this tank is badly hurt, and how badly.

B's job, condition h <= 0.6, amount_ratio follows health, wreck 1.0

beats.role_note: Code beat: effects/damage_smoke.tscn lines 47-58 (the GPUParticles2D node), verbatim; process lines 30-32 and draw lines 4/7 in notes.
beats.narration_text: Three parts. Emission: amount forty eight, lifetime one point six. Process: velocity and gravity, which become shader lines. Draw: a soft dot texture, blend mix, a visibility rect.

beats.role_note: Verdict: mistakes caught both ways, the overruled reading, uncertainty, next step, contributions, textures, revision.
beats.narration_text: The verdict, at commit four one a six b eight b. The student caught a cost script measuring itself, a false uncommitted claim, inferred exit codes, and frozen test enemies. The agent caught three problems in the brief. Claude Code built, Claude chat drafted, the student judged. Next: lower B's turbulence.

artifactLines: Caught by the student: cost script measuring itself · "R5 uncommitted" (it was 96d38be) · exit codes the agent could only infer · tests that froze enemies (no bodies, stopped timers), fixed in tests only.
Caught by the agent in the brief: old debris gravity (0, 160) · the null-shell test break · 0.94 vs 0.875.
Strip reading overruled: Effect B r1 ("prediction failed"); in the game it rises — kept.
Uncertain: turbulence as the cause is confirmed from code, not by a turbulence-off strip · leak counts vary.
Next step: lower B's turbulence influence, or lighten its base colour.
Claude Code: effects, tests, previews · Claude chat: brief, scripts, documents · the student: approved every step, ran every test and capture, made every verdict.
Textures: chip_6.png, soft_dot_32.png, drawn by code · no downloaded or AI textures.
